title: Review of c14's pdrop arrested-emulsion negative: replicated on fresh seed 7 (98 static droplets, 2 persistent splits, generation 1) and still arrested after 4x the time on seed 8 (80000 steps: 100 droplets, 2 persistent splits)
summary: The claim's world.py at its published defaults (F 0.01, Du 0.3) on two fresh seeds. Seed 7 with the claim's pack settings (20000 steps, time 10000): from a near-uniform soup about 100 droplets appear within ~1000 t and sit as a packed emulsion (components mean 97.9, final 100, occupancy 0.30; 7 splits, 2 persistent, max generation 1, 23 merges; rerun/seed7/sheet.png). Seed 8 run four times longer (80000 steps, time 40000; long/seed8/sheet.png): the emulsion is frozen in the same state from t~7000 to 40000 (mean 99.5 components, final 100, 6 splits, 2 persistent, generation 1, 21 merges), so the arrest is not a transient of the reported window. I did not repeat the parameter screen.

observations.finding: rerun/seed7/FACTS.md: 2 persistent splits, max generation 1, merge/split 3.29, ~100 droplets throughout; long/seed8/sheet.png: the same packed emulsion of ~100 droplets from t=7000 to t=40000 with no growth-division cycle (2 persistent splits, generation 1)

seeds_run.result: pass: arrested to time 40000 (4x the reported window)

controls_run.finding: long/seed8: the same world run 4x longer

verdicts.limitation: Only the published default setting was re-run (the 10 other screen settings were not); occupancy is 0.30 with droplets nearly touching, so arrest may partly be crowding: a sparser setting that keeps the particles alive was not found by the claim and not tried here.
